stories.headline: Beijing condemns Lai Ching-te for 'glorifying Japanese colonial rule' in speech
stories.summary: Chinese officials accused Taiwan President Lai Ching-te of 'glorifying Japanese colonial rule' after he made comparisons between early KMT rule and the Japanese colonial period, calling it worse than colonial rule. Beijing denounced this as an attempt to distort history and seek Taiwan independence.

stories.headline: Premier Cho Jung-tai's Japan baseball trip sparks political controversy
stories.summary: Premier Cho Jung-tai's personally-funded trip to Tokyo to watch Taiwan's World Baseball Classic game drew criticism and scrutiny from political opponents. Cho defended the trip as 'baseball diplomacy' and paid for personally, marking the first such visit by Taiwan leadership since 1972.

stories.headline: TSMC chairman dismisses Chinese robotics capabilities, touts chip dominance
stories.summary: TSMC Chairman C.C. Wei dismissed Chinese robots as 'useless' and emphasized Taiwan's dominance in manufacturing AI chips, stating that 95% of robot 'brains' are manufactured by TSMC. Wei made these comments while receiving an honorary degree and discussing Taiwan's technological leadership.

stories.headline: KMT-TPP approve cooperation pact for local elections
stories.summary: Taiwan's main opposition KMT and the smaller TPP approved a cooperation agreement for local elections, agreeing to jointly field candidates and coordinate in areas where both parties have nominees including New Taipei, Yilan County and other constituencies.

articles.title: KMT, TPP approve cooperation pact for local elections

stories.headline: Prosecutors raid KMT councilor's office in corruption probe
stories.summary: Taipei prosecutors searched the office and residence of KMT Taipei City Councilor Lee Fu Chung-wu over alleged corruption tied to fraudulent assistant expense claims. Lee is a fourth-term councilor and former police officer who previously served on the KMT Central Standing Committee.

articles.title: Prosecutors raid KMT Taipei councilor's office

stories.headline: Premier announces UAV industry development and migrant worker expansion
stories.summary: Premier Cho Jung-tai announced plans to cultivate Taiwan's drone industry over five years with NT$44.2 billion in funding to create a non-red supply chain. He also approved expanding eligibility for migrant domestic helpers with new monthly fees for employers.
